practice.development[3]: The booklet displays simulation histograms but never asks students to infer a limiting value from a supplied relative-frequency line graph or name the law from that graph. Replace this off-booklet task with a supported Development task and update its structure slug; the solution also incorrectly implies that successive estimates necessarily become closer.

practice.development[4]: Part a is a supported observed-probability calculation. Part b is not a question type asked in the supplied booklet and falsely requires observed probability because no theoretical value exists; remove that part and its explanation while preserving part a.

practice.development[5]: Change the solution's claim that recording more trials necessarily makes the estimate closer to the true probability to an expectation of greater reliability; convergence need not be monotonic.

practice.mastery[1]: The source asks which statement about the biased die is correct, not for the probability of another face; that calculation occurs only inside its solution (Booklet 1, lines 1869–1886). Part b also introduces complementary-probability inference beyond the target skill; replace it with a supported Mastery observed-probability task and update the structure slug.

practice.mastery[2]: The source's simulation figures illustrate teaching but do not ask students to describe a supplied sequence or infer its limiting probability. Replace this off-booklet task with a supported Mastery task and update its structure slug; if retaining any theoretical-probability statement, specify a fair die rather than assuming fairness from finite results.

quiz.q8: Estimating probability from a supplied cumulative relative-frequency line graph is not asked anywhere in the supplied booklet. Replace this question with an adapted supported task, preserve id q8 and mastery:true, and update the structure slug; the solution also overstates what this finite graph establishes about convergence.

theory: Replace the assertion that unequal outcomes have no theoretical probability with the statement that their probabilities may be unknown and can be estimated from repeated trials. Replace 'usually close but rarely equal' with a statement that observed and theoretical probabilities can differ through randomness, especially with few trials; describe greater reliability with more trials without implying guaranteed improvement at every increase. Theoretical probability is model-based, not defined by whether calculation occurs before trials.
summary: Replaced four off-booklet tasks with supported product-sales, missing-frequency and survey-prediction questions, updated their structure slugs and supplied source citations; removed only part b of practice.development[4], preserving part a. Corrected the theory and affected explanations about unknown probabilities and greater reliability without guaranteed successive improvement, while preserving the remaining items and values.
reviewSummary: All eight requested items have correct answers, appropriate Stage 4 methods and question types explicitly asked in the booklet. The theory accurately explains observed probability, prediction from relative frequency and the Law of Large Numbers; no repairs or removals are required.
